requirements.requirement: Create a local account named `opsadmin` on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was created locally and, after reboot, resolved as UID/GID 1001 with `/home/opsadmin`, `/bin/bash`, wheel membership, and an active password.
Post-reboot inspection shows `/home/opsadmin` is a directory owned by `opsadmin:opsadmin` with mode 0700.
The validated sudoers policy permits all commands as all users and groups, and an actual post-reboot sudo invocation by `opsadmin` returned effective UID 0.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged a scheduled restart, changed from boot ID `fe6e58b2-7e4d-4e8a-b1d7-3a15564059bb` to `136c6d29-6515-4920-b082-9309d473cea6`, returned to a running state, retained the account/home/sudoers data, and successfully performed post-reboot root elevation. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account, home, password, and sudoers changes directly established or validated the requested administrator. Password rotations supported direct sudo behavior tests; temporary sudoers and boot-ID files were removed. The reboot and transient scheduling were required evidence-protocol actions. Afterward, node1 had no failed services, unchanged socket exposure, healthy package state, and no executor-created temporary-file residue.
